references.text: Moses is told to take off his sandals because the place where he stands is holy ground, just as Joshua receives the same command in the next verse (Josh 5:15).
Michael is described as one of the chief princes and may be the same heavenly commander who appears to Joshua.
Michael is called the prince of Israel, which links him to the role of the Lord's commander.
Michael is described as the great prince who stands guard over God's people, a parallel to the commander who appears to Joshua.
Abraham falls down before the three men who visit him, a similar gesture of reverence shown by Joshua.
Jacob wrestles with a heavenly being and sees God face to face, a divine confrontation similar to what Joshua experiences.
John falls down before the angel but is told not to worship him. This contrasts with Joshua's worship, which is accepted.
Michael and his angels fight in heaven, a parallel to the commander of the Lord's army.
Jesus is called the leader of their salvation, a title that recalls the commander of the Lord's army.
